question: Has Workday announced any restructuring recently? What are the details and expected costs?
grading: Reference-free (no fixed answer), graded for recency and support. Expect: announced 2026-09-29; reorganizations including a reduction of approximately 2.5% of the workforce, primarily in Product and Technology, plus select leased office space reductions; estimated charges USD 65M-80M (about USD 55M-70M in Q3 FY2027 and about USD 10M in Q4 FY2027); fiscal 2027 Q3 and full-year guidance reiterated except GAAP operating margin. Snapshot as of 2026-10-03.
answer: On September 29, 2026 Workday disclosed in an 8-K (Items 2.02 and 2.05) that certain functions announced reorganizations including a reduction of approximately 2.5% of its workforce, primarily within the Product and Technology team, and select leased office space reductions, while continuing to hire in strategic areas. It estimates charges of about USD 65-80 million, of which about USD 55-70 million in Q3 FY2027 and about USD 10 million in Q4 FY2027 (roughly USD 40-55 million future cash for severance and benefits, about USD 10 million non-cash stock-based compensation and about USD 15 million non-cash lease impairment). Workday reiterated its Q3 and full-year FY2027 guidance from August 27 except GAAP operating margin (now about 20-21 points below non-GAAP in Q3 and about 19 points below for the full year). [T16-E1, T16-E2] Separately, on October 1, 2026 Workday entered into a new USD 1.5 billion revolving credit agreement replacing its USD 1.0 billion 2022 facility; this is not part of the restructuring. [T16-E3]

output.answer:
Yes. Workday has announced restructurings over the past year. The most recent was filed in **February 2026**, and there was a larger plan announced in **February 2025**.

### February 2026 Restructuring (Most Recent)
- **Scope:** About **400 job cuts** (~2% of the workforce), primarily in **Global Customer Operations** and other customer-facing, non-revenue generating roles.
- **Purpose:** To “better align their people and resources to their highest priorities in fiscal 2027.”
- **Expected Cost:** Approximately **$135 million** in restructuring and impairment charges. This includes an **$80 million impairment charge** related to office space consolidation. Workday cautioned actual costs could exceed the estimate.
- **Timeline:** Expected to be largely completed by **late April 2026**.
- **Leadership Context:** This announcement coincided with the resignation of CEO Carl Eschenbach, who had stepped in during 2024 and overseen the earlier restructuring.

### February 2025 Restructuring (Fiscal 2026 Plan)
- **Scope:** A reduction of approximately **7.5% to 8.5%** of the workforce, or about **1,750 employees**. The company also exited certain owned office space.
- **Purpose:** To prioritize investments in AI and durable growth.
- **Recorded Costs (through fiscal 2026):** 
  - **$133 million** for employee transition, severance, benefits, and share-based compensation (during the nine months ended October 31, 2025).
  - **$39 million** for impairment of office space.
  - For the full fiscal year 2026, share-based compensation associated with restructuring activities totaled **$56 million**.

**Sources:**  
- [Workday Fiscal 2026 Q3 Results (investor.workday.com)](https://investor.workday.com/news-and-events/press-releases/news-details/2025/Workday-Announces-Fiscal-2026-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results-11-25-2025/default.aspx)  
- [Workday CEO Steps Down Amid Layoffs (The Register)](https://www.theregister.com/off-prem/2026/02/09/workday-ceo-steps-down-amid-layoffs-and-market-jitters/4539088)  
- [Workday Files More Job Cuts; Customer Ops Hit (HR Executive)](https://hrexecutive.com/workday-files-more-job-cuts-customer-ops-teams-hit)  
- [Business Insider Layoffs List 2026](https://www.businessinsider.com/recent-company-layoffs-laying-off-workers-2026)
